input: Prepare me for a meeting with Gong (gong.io)

talking_points: With Gong Activate and the new R&D leadership, which agent-driven workflows are the next priority—and how will you measure their business impact?
As Gong Enrich expands the data foundation, how are you addressing integration friction and making licensing and usage costs clear to customers?
Following the Klue incident and Guy Havusha’s CISO appointment, what additional controls are priorities for third-party integrations and agents acting on customer data?

key_people.title: CEO & Co-Founder
key_people.recent: On November 4, 2026, said Gong’s next phase is agents that take action and deliver results at enterprise scale, rather than just surface insights.
key_people.name: Amit Bendov

key_people.title: Chief R&D Officer
key_people.recent: Appointed November 4, 2026, to lead R&D and expand agentic capabilities across Gong’s Revenue Graph, Revenue Harness and Revenue Operating Surfaces.
key_people.name: Liron Shtraichman

key_people.title: Chief Information Security Officer
key_people.recent: Named CISO on November 4, 2026, after serving as VP of Platform Security; leads global security, privacy and compliance as Gong expands AI-agent execution.
key_people.name: Guy Havusha

missing_fields: challenges.current_status: Whether the April 2026 customer complaints persist as of November 9, 2026, could not be verified. The security incident below is historical; Klue reported integration restoration in July.

challenges.evidence: Gong disclosed that an unauthorized actor accessed third-party integrator Klue’s integration service, potentially exposing some connected customers’ internal licensed-user names, business titles and emails. Gong said this was not a direct breach of its products or systems and identified no direct impact to call recordings or transcripts. This is a historical security exposure, not a confirmed ongoing outage: Klue reported restoration on July 27, 2026 (https://klue.com/blog/integrations-restored-salesforce-and-gong-reconnected).
challenges.challenge: Third-party integration security exposure and associated customer-data risk.

challenges.evidence: An April 15, 2026 Gartner Peer Insights review criticized limited integration and additional fees for core features. An April 29, 2026 favorable review nevertheless described licensing as costly and complex. These are individual customer opinions, not proof of a systemic problem or its persistence today.
challenges.challenge: Documented customer friction around interoperability, licensing complexity and additional fees.

what_they_do.value: Gong Revenue AI unifies data, insights, and workflows into a single, trusted system that observes, guides, and acts alongside the world’s most successful revenue teams.

recent_changes.headline: Gong appoints new R&D and security leaders.
recent_changes.summary: Liron Shtraichman was appointed Chief R&D Officer and Guy Havusha was named CISO, supporting expanded agentic capabilities and enterprise security.

recent_changes.headline: Gong announces Activate and its self-improving revenue loop.
recent_changes.summary: Activate brings agents and revenue teams together around shared account motions, with outcomes feeding back into the Revenue Graph. The release announces the product but does not establish general availability.

recent_changes.headline: Gong introduces Enrich, Agent Builder and Deep Mode.
recent_changes.summary: Enrich fills missing account and contact details; Agent Builder creates event-triggered custom agents; Deep Mode investigates complex business questions within Gong Assistant.

priorities.evidence: The new R&D leader’s stated remit is expanding agentic capabilities across Gong’s core platform. Amit Bendov described the next phase as agents that take action and deliver results at enterprise scale.
priorities.priority: Expand agentic Revenue AI from insights into enterprise-scale execution.

priorities.evidence: Gong introduced Enrich to fill missing account and contact details, expanding the Revenue Graph with richer third-party data and reducing sellers’ research work.
priorities.priority: Strengthen the account-and-contact data foundation through Gong Enrich.

priorities.evidence: Gong named Guy Havusha CISO with responsibility for global security, privacy and compliance. His remit explicitly makes data security and governance differentiators as AI agents take on more revenue-cycle work.
priorities.priority: Make enterprise security and governance central to AI-agent adoption.

citations.title: Gong Strengthens Leadership Team with Appointment of Liron Shtraichman as Chief R&D Officer
excerpts: **SAN FRANCISCO — November 4, 2026** —Gong, the leader in revenue AI, today announced the appointment of [Liron Shtraichman](https://www.linkedin.com/in/liron-shtraichman-3919015a/) as Chief R&D (research & development) Officer and [Guy Havusha](https://www.linkedin.com/in/guy-havusha/) as Chief Information Security Officer (CISO

The next phase is about agents that don’t just surface insights, but take action and deliver results at enterprise scale,” said Amit Bendov, CEO and co-founder of Gong. “Liron has scaled a global engineering organization and led a full transition to AI-native development. And with Guy leading security, our customers can put AI agents to work knowing their data is protected to the highest enterprise standards. That’s exactly the experience to keep transforming how revenue teams win.

This experience will be invaluable at Gong, where he will lead R&D and be focused on expanding the agentic capabilities Gong delivers to leading revenue teams across its Revenue Graph, Revenue Harness, Revenue Operating Surfaces and more.
Previously serving as Vice President of Platform Security at Gong, Havusha now takes the reins as CISO, a role he is familiar with, having also previously served as Global CISO at monday.com.
As CISO, Havusha leads Gong’s global security, privacy, and compliance programs, ensuring that the customer data powering Gong’s AI and the agents acting on it meet the highest enterprise standards.

basis.reasoning: The November 4 company announcement directly supplies the appointments, titles, responsibilities and CEO statement. The current About page also lists these leaders.
The opened review evidence is dated April. No opened source established whether those complaints remained unresolved in November; this is a research limitation, not an assertion about the company.

citations.title: Klue Security Incident | Gong
excerpts: Published on: June 19, 2026
To be clear: this was an incident that originated with third-party integrator Klue. It was not a direct breach of Gong’s own products or systems.
Gong has not identified any direct impact to customer call recordings or transcripts.

Based upon those IP Addresses and information available at this time, we can confirm that a subset of customers using the Klue integration may have had internal licensed user data accessed, though we can confirm no direct impact on call recordings or customer transcripts. Examples of data accessed included user names, user business titles and user emails
